report.source_text: Serial MRI brain scans at presentation (A–C), 3 months (D–F) and 6 months (G–I) following initial presentation in a child with Baló’s concentric sclerosis. The initial MRI with contrast demonstrated a T2 hyperintense abnormality with central hypointense ring-like focus (A); alternating layers of high and low signal intensity giving it an ‘onion bulb’ appearance. There was central concentric contrast enhancement (B). At 3 months, the extent of the abnormality (D) and the area of contrast enhancement (E) had increased. At 6 months, the abnormality (G) and the contrast enhancement (H) had resolved. The abnormality showed central diffusion restriction with unrestricted diffusion in the periphery (C). The area of diffusion restriction increased in size at 3 months (F) and disappeared by 6 months (I).

clinician.trajectory_summary: An asymptomatic school-aged boy was incidentally found to have possible papilloedema leading to a non-enhanced head CT that revealed a hyperdense left posterior frontal lobe lesion with surrounding oedema. MRI brain showed a characteristic lesion with alternating concentric rings of high and low signal intensity and central contrast enhancement, consistent with Baló’s concentric sclerosis. Serial MRI at 3 and 6 months demonstrated progression and then resolution of the abnormality and contrast enhancement. Repeat imaging at 3 months showed lesion growth prompting biopsy. Histopathological examination confirmed the lesion as a demyelinating inflammatory lesion consistent with Baló’s concentric sclerosis. The child was managed conservatively with lesion resolution on imaging.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Initial non-enhanced CT showed a hyperdense lesion in the left posterior frontal lobe with surrounding hypodensity suggesting oedema.

MRI brain demonstrated a lesion with characteristic alternating concentric rings of T2 hyperintensity and hypointensity with central contrast enhancement and diffusion restriction evolving over 6 months, consistent with Baló’s concentric sclerosis.
Repeat imaging at 3 months showed lesion growth and changes in signal characteristics prompting biopsy to exclude tumor.
Histopathological examination of biopsy confirmed a demyelinating inflammatory lesion, consistent with Baló’s concentric sclerosis (final diagnosis).
